history.author: fable-cursor
history.criterion: Trunks are irregular, tapered, leaning, with hierarchical branches — recognisably the Verdant white trees, better.
history.note: No trunk at C reads as a tapered, leaning, hierarchically branched white-bark tree. The visible near white-bark at the right edge is a straight untapered pale pole with no flare and no branch structure, and the whole background layer behind it is a wall of flat grey-blue polygonal cards with straight cut edges and angular notches, with no trunk-and-limb structure at all (see take-0116-W08b-C-background-trunks.jpg). Measured, that band is #535a5a with sigma 23.6 against the reference's #6e6c60 with sigma 11.4: ours carries twice the local contrast because the card edges are hard, where the reference's hazed crown is soft and shows a real branching silhouette. Auto gates are met (10 variants, 78 instances, geometry procedural-v1).

history.note: Every white-bark visible in the six frames - C right (x 0.90-0.98, y 0.15-0.50), the B/E background (x 0.15-0.35, y 0.0-0.40), D left (x 0.10-0.35, y 0.0-0.55) - is a straight, near-vertical, smooth pale pole with faint grey bands and no root flare; the one horizontal limb at C is a smooth sausage with sparse leaf cards stuck along it.
